title: Accepted-origin q(H) and directional response sampling
purpose: Measure interface exchange as a function of prescribed groundwater head from an unchanged accepted origin, and compare the transaction-published accepted-trajectory derivative with a centered finite difference where both sides accept.

scope.base_heads: The actual MODFLOW trial heads frozen in the C0/C1 first-window result
scope.independent_origin: Each probe starts from the same pristine committed origin in a fresh initialized backend; a rejected or accepted candidate is discarded and never committed.

measurements: canonical transaction status, accepted substeps, attempts/retries and solver/temporal/mass/admission rejection counts
bottom interface exchange integrated over the accepted trial and terminal bottom outward flux in native units
accepted trajectory derivative availability, accepted steps, derivative value and route/method
committed physical state and revisions before/after

analysis.finite_difference: Compute a centered derivative only if both +/-1e-8 m probes accept from the same origin and their sign/unit mapping is source-verified. Otherwise mark unavailable.
analysis.admission: No admission threshold is widened and no rejected candidate substitutes for an ordinary transaction.

interpretation_limits: This is a local response diagnostic, not a coupled-window qualification.
An available directional derivative is accepted only for its named control coordinate, units, interval and route; it is not assumed to be d(qbot)/d(head).
Do not infer whole-domain mass closure, Hupsel readiness or production admission.

implementation_boundary.changes: Research fixture only; no shared source, contract, acceptance policy or production adapter changes.
